newsitem.title: USA: Globalstar junk deal soars in US corporate mart.
newsitem.headline: Globalstar junk deal soars in US corporate mart.

text.p: Globalstar L.P. set off rockets in the the U.S. corporate bond market on Thursday with its first high-yield bond offering, market players said.
Supercharged demand from investors led the company to double the size of the offering to $500 million from $250 million. Lehman Brothers Inc served as the underwriter.
Globalstar is a partnership of 12 telephone companies building a global mobile satellite telephone system.
Market players said the success of the offering was particuraly notable, given the fact that the Globalstar pulled the deal last year due to a lack of investor interest.
Analysts and investors sympathetic to the deal said prospects for Globalstar have improved since that time.
They noted since the original offering, Globalstar has raised more capital from banks and investors and has received authorizations to operate in more countries, such as China.
Globalstar has also made progress on constructing its satellites, the first of which is scheduled to be lauched in the third quarter of 1997, they said.
Globalstar, like other junk issuers, certainly benefitted from currently strong market technicals fueled by continued cash inflows into high-yield mutual funds, they said.
The Globalstar offering consisted of units composed of senior notes due 2004 and warrants. The warrants totalled 1.78 percent of the company.
Traders reported heavy trading of the issue in the secondary market on Thursday. The units, which were priced at par, were quoted at 103 1/4 in the afternoon, they said.
Elsewhere, Sun Media Corp, a Toronto-based newpaper publishing group, sold $150 million in senior subordinated notes due 2007 via CIBC Wood Gundy Securities on Thursday.
Traders said the bonds, which priced at par, were trading at 101 1/4 soon after they priced.

In the secondary market, traders said the junk bonds of Harvard Industries Inc, an automobile parts maker, opened around five points lower on Thursday morning after the company reported lower-than expected earnings on Wednesday night.
The bonds, which closed at 71 on Wednesday, opened at 65 3/4, a trader said. The bonds rose to 66-67 later in the day.
Traders said overall prices in the junk market rose by 1/8 to 1/4 of a point on moderate trading activity on Thursday.
The high-grade market also saw better buying on Thursday, with traders reporting bond spreads tighter by one-half a basis point on average.
In the Treasury market, the U.S. Treasury completed its quarterly refunding by selling $10.0 billion in 30-year bonds on Thursday.
The price of the benchmark 30-year Treasury rose one point to 98.11, pushing the yield down to 6.63 percent.
